Bootloaders

If you didnt already choose a firmware interface for your os, go to Getting Started and choose one, we recommend you choose one based on your OSes needs and not code complexity

BIOS

A BIOS reads the first sector of your drive, checks if the last 2 bytes match the boot signature 0x55 0xAA, if they are valid, it loads those 512 bytes into memory at 0x7C00 and executes it. That is your bootloader code, usually 440-446 bytes free for machine code in the bootloader (When counting for MBR partition tables).

This is the simplest bootloader, we set nasm origin to 0x7c00 and pad it to 510 bytes with 0s, last 2 is the boot signature. If the BIOS expects a MBR partition table (most likely when booting on real hardware) your code would look like
